summary: This is an Emergen Research market report page on the global incident and emergency management market, published June 2022 (Report ID ER_001043, 250 pages). It states the market was USD 124.68 billion in 2021 with a 7.0% revenue CAGR through 2030, driven by government disaster-management investment, terror and cyber threats, and natural disasters, while high maintenance costs and lack of education and training restrain growth. It also covers segments (system type, service, communication technology, simulation, vertical, region), regional trends, leading companies, and recent industry news.
one_line: Emergen Research's 2022 report forecasting the global incident and emergency management market to reach USD 226.93 billion by 2030.
key_facts: The global incident and emergency management market size was USD 124.68 Billion in 2021.
The incident and emergency management market is expected to register a revenue CAGR of 7.0% during the forecast period (2022–2030).
The revenue forecast for the incident and emergency management market in 2030 is USD 226.93 Billion.
The report was published in June 2022 with Report ID ER_001043 and runs to 250 pages.
The fire and HAZMAT segment accounted for a significantly large revenue share in 2021.
The incident and evacuation simulation tools segment accounted for the largest revenue share in the simulation segment.
The satellite-assisted equipment segment was the leading communication technology segment in terms of revenue share in 2021.
The BFSI segment accounted for the largest revenue share by vertical in 2021.
The North America market accounted for the highest revenue growth in 2021, while Europe accounted for the second-largest revenue share.
On 5 August 2021, Accenture and the Fire Department of City of New York (FDNY) developed a new Computer-Aided Dispatch system named FireCAD, which replaced the STARFIRE system.
On 9 June 2021, Honeywell International Inc. launched Advanced Monitoring and Incident Response (AMIR) services.
On 23 May 2022, AiDash launched its Disaster and Disruption Management System (DDMS).
High cost of maintenance and lack of proper education and training are key factors hampering market growth, according to the report.
The report lists twelve key companies profiled, including Honeywell International Inc., Lockheed Martin Corporation, Siemens, IBM and Motorola Solutions, Inc.
